clue.text: Russian drink: last of that very thick one

parts.note: 'that' points back to the word drink just used, and its last letter is K
a thick, dim person is an ass

explanation.surface: A note on some heavy Russian beverage, the final one of which is the most viscous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that' does not mean itself here: it stands for the word 'drink' earlier in the clue, so 'last of that' gives the K at the end of drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Kvass is a mildly alcoholic fermented beverage made from rye bread, traditional in Russia.

clue.text: Look back over young professional footballer's skilful display

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed on top
back means read the word for look in reverse

parts.note: to peek is to take a quick look
a yuppy is a young urban professional

explanation.surface: A scout reviewing a young pro footballer's showreel.
explanation.definitionFit: Keepy-uppy is juggling a football in the air without letting it touch the ground, a show of ball skill.

clue.text: First-rate record hard for motorists to surpass

indicators.note: to go over and around, so the motoring body sits on both sides of the other pieces

parts.note: the AA is the Automobile Association, a British motoring organisation
an LP is a long-playing record
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A top-class driving record that other motorists struggle to beat.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA is the UK's Automobile Association, a breakdown service for motorists.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha is the top grade in marking, so an alpha result is first-rate.

clue.text: Figures from Rome are stopping crime of Mafia origin

indicators.note: the numerals stop, or plug, the word for crime, going inside it

parts.note: a sin is a wrongdoing
C, I, L, I are all Roman numerals
A is the abbreviation for are, a unit of area

explanation.surface: Roman police figures are halting organised crime.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mafia began in Sicily. 'are' gives A because an are is a metric unit of area, a hundred square metres.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mafia began in Sicily, so something of Mafia origin can be called Sicilian.

clue.text: Experimental poet's revolutionary articles for the well-groomed?

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns right round, so the two pieces before it are read backwards as one run

parts.note: test, as in a test run, means experimental
T. S. Eliot is the poet

explanation.surface: A radical poet's avant-garde work promoted to grooming products.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns the whole run TESTELIOT backwards, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A toilet set is a matching kit of brush, comb and mirror used for grooming, so its items suit the well-groomed.

clue.text: Spot on top of ermine's vanished

indicators.note: the top of a down entry is its first letter
the first letter disappears from the animal's name

parts.note: an ermine is a stoat in its white winter coat

explanation.surface: A dark mark on an ermine's head has disappeared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spot' looks like a noun, a mark on the fur, but 'Spot on' means exactly right.
explanation.definitionFit: To a T is an idiom meaning precisely, exactly right, just as spot on does.

clue.text: Faltering guards pursuing one won't, strangely

indicators.note: pursuing means coming after, so the guards follow the other pieces

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: strangely says the letters of won't are put in an odd order

parts.note: to mind is to guard, so minds means guards

explanation.surface: Wavering security guards chasing someone who refuses, oddly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' turns WONT into NTWO.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in two minds means undecided and wavering, so faltering in resolve.

clue.text: Porter comes up with notice well concealed in one

indicators.note: the note is hidden away inside the reversed composer's name
in a down clue, coming up means the word is read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: Cole Porter was the American songwriter
NB stands for nota bene, Latin for note well

explanation.surface: A doorman turns up with a note tucked away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porter' looks like a doorman, but it is Cole Porter. 'comes up' gives ELOC.
explanation.definitionFit: En bloc means all together as a single unit, i.e. in one.

clue.text: Tie with notches on both sides?

definitions.text: Tie with notches on both sides?

parts.words: Tie with notches on both sides?
parts.note: read as a necktie or rope with cuts, but really a football result where each team scores, notches being tallied goals

explanation.walkthrough: A notch is a tally mark, so a score; a drawn match where both teams score is the British football pools term.
explanation.definitionFit: A score draw is a drawn football match in which both teams have scored, a tie with goals on both sides.

clue.text: First of December every year our tax return fiddled

indicators.note: a tax return here signals the collected letters are turned back
takes the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Every year at the start of December our tax return gets doctored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First of' takes D, E, Y, O, T; 'return' reverses them.
explanation.definitionFit: To toy with something is to fiddle with it idly, so toyed means fiddled.

clue.text: In the club, still there's muscle to be brought in

indicators.note: the muscle is brought in, so it goes inside the word for still existing

parts.note: extant means still in existence, still there
pec is short for pectoral muscle

explanation.surface: At the gym, a muscle still needs to be worked in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the club' is British slang for pregnant, not a place to exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: 'In the club' is informal British slang for pregnant, and an expectant mother is one who is pregnant.

clue.text: Alcoholic youth touring Australia

indicators.note: the youth tours round, so his word goes around the abbreviation for Australia

parts.note: a youth is a boy
Oz is a common informal name for Australia

explanation.surface: A drunk young backpacker travelling around Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Boozy is an adjective for drinking a lot of alcohol, matching alcoholic in the sense of drink-fuelled.

clue.text: Unknown in advance, like circulation of the Sun?

parts.note: Y is one of the algebraic letters standing for an unknown quantity
early means ahead of time, in advance

explanation.surface: An astronomer muses about what is not yet known regarding the Sun's cycle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sun's apparent circuit of the sky through the zodiac takes one year, so it happens annually.

clue.text: Decline to visit daughter

parts.note: to go to see someone is to visit them

explanation.surface: Someone refusing an invitation to call on their daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decline' looks like a verb of refusing; here it means to deteriorate.
explanation.definitionFit: To go to seed is an idiom for deteriorating or letting oneself go, i.e. declining.

clue.text: Battle is something dentist fights with whisky drinking

indicators.note: the whisky drinks, taking the other piece inside it

parts.note: malt is a single-malt whisky
plaque is the deposit on teeth dentists combat

explanation.surface: A dentist battles his patient's whisky habit.
explanation.walkthrough: Malplaquet (1709) was one of Marlborough's battles against the French.
explanation.definitionFit: Malplaquet was a 1709 battle of the War of the Spanish Succession, won by Marlborough at great cost.

clue.text: Indian gentleman's hollow knock as a greeting in tavern

indicators.note: the pieces are placed inside the word for a tavern

parts.note: a tavern is a pub

indicators.note: a hollow word has had its insides removed, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: hi is an informal greeting

explanation.surface: A colonial figure knocks on a pub door by way of saying hello.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hollow' keeps only K and K of knock.
explanation.definitionFit: Pukka sahib was the colonial Indian term for a proper or genuine gentleman, especially a European one.

clue.text: It's linked with reform, as most charitable bodies are

indicators.note: to reform is to reshape, so the letters of the phrase are rearranged

explanation.surface: A charity is connected to reform, as most charitable organisations are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with reform' rearranges ITSLINKED.
explanation.definitionFit: Charitable organisations aim to be the kindest, most benevolent, which is what kindliest describes.

clue.text: I bore pop group's leader with endless tirade

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
the synonym for tirade loses its final letter

parts.note: a rant is a tirade

explanation.surface: Someone moaning that a pop band's frontman bored them with an interminable rant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pop' is father here, not music: a woman who bore someone's father is his grandmother.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandmother is the mother who gave birth to one's pop, i.e. one's father, so she could say she bore him.

clue.text: Toff and Prince, the second I disappeared, making easy choice

parts.note: a nob is a posh, upper-class person, a toff

indicators.note: the second letter I is removed from the prince's name

parts.note: Prince Rainier ruled Monaco

explanation.surface: An aristocrat and a prince, with one going missing, making an obvious decision.
explanation.walkthrough: TOFF and NOB are British slang for a posh person. Prince Rainier III of Monaco lost his second I, leaving RAINER.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-brainer is a decision so obvious it needs no thought, an easy choice.

clue.text: Still lag behind after capturing knight and queen

indicators.note: the lagging word captures the chess pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: to trail is to lag behind
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A chess player falls behind after the opponent takes a knight and queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' is an adjective meaning calm, not an adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: Tranquil means calm and peaceful, which is what still means as an adjective.

clue.text: Couple bidding to follow the second person's desires

indicators.note: the bidding couple come after, so they are placed after the other piece

parts.note: ye is the old second-person plural pronoun, meaning you
North and South are partners in bridge, bidding as a pair

explanation.surface: A pair at an auction wanting to outbid what the runner-up wants.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge North and South (N, S) are a partnership, so a bidding couple is NS; YE is the archaic second-person pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: A yen is a longing or yearning, so yens are desires.

clue.text: It's dangerous to fly: wind sweeps bird about

indicators.note: to wind is to twist about, signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Flying is hazardous: the gale is blowing a bird around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fly' reads as a verb, but it is the insect: a web is dangerous for a fly.
explanation.definitionFit: A web spun by a spider traps and kills insects, so it is a hazard for a fly.

clue.text: Drop major news item

explanation.definitionFit: A splash is a little liquid added, and in journalism a splash is the lead story given big headlines.

clue.text: Acting with bold heart in attempt to resolve 7

indicators.note: the heart is put inside the word for the second attempt

parts.note: a replay is the rematch that settles a drawn football tie, the answer to 7

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letters

explanation.surface: Performing with brave spirit in a bid to settle a deadlock.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 is the score draw; a drawn cup tie is settled by a replay. 'heart' gives OL from bold.
explanation.definitionFit: Role-play is acting out a part, so it is a form of acting.

clue.text: Undoing wrong at last, or wishing one could

parts.note: someone's undoing is their ruin

indicators.note: takes the final letter of the word wrong

explanation.surface: Regretting the downfall of doing wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the clue before it: wishing one could undo the wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: To rue is to regret, wishing one could undo something, so ruing describes that regret.

clue.text: Find a bar to hold conference

indicators.note: the words find a bar hold the answer inside them

explanation.surface: Looking for a pub where a meeting can take place.
explanation.walkthrough: f(INDABA)r: the answer sits inside 'Find a bar'.
explanation.definitionFit: An indaba is a southern African word for a meeting or conference, originally of tribal elders.

clue.text: Article by Shelley where he fails to show great depth

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: the letters he are missing from the poet's middle name

parts.note: Percy Bysshe Shelley was the Romantic poet

explanation.surface: A piece by Shelley in which the man himself never appears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' looks like part of the wordplay but is a link; it is Shelley's middle name, Bysshe, that loses HE.
explanation.definitionFit: An abyss is a seemingly bottomless chasm, so it is a great depth.

clue.text: Tramp over fine pile of leaves

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above

parts.note: a bum is a tramp
F is the pencil abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A vagrant sleeping on a heap of autumn leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' are sheets of paper, not foliage.
explanation.definitionFit: Bumf is British slang for paperwork, a pile of leaves in the sense of sheets of paper.

clue.text: Miss seeing red heart of cinnabar

parts.note: seeing red is being angry, and ire is anger

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letters

explanation.surface: A young woman glimpsing the red core of a mineral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' is a girl, so it defines a girl's name; cinnabar is a red mineral, which helps the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Irena is a woman's first name, and Miss is the title for an unmarried girl, so a girl's name fits.

clue.text: No to the French teacher going over Latin!

indicators.note: going over suggests turning right round, so the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: nay means no
au is French for to the
a guru is a spiritual teacher

explanation.surface: A French lesson where the teacher refuses to cover Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going over' turns NAYAUGURU backwards. 'Latin' is not the language but a Latin American.
explanation.definitionFit: A Uruguayan comes from a Latin American country, so is a Latin in that sense.

clue.text: Kick and is kicked by horse? About time!

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the horse phrase goes around the time letter

parts.note: someone kicked by a horse gets hoof

explanation.surface: A rider complaining of being kicked by a horse and saying it took long enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kick' is to give up a habit, not to strike.
explanation.definitionFit: To kick a habit is to get rid of it, and get shot of is British slang for getting rid of something.

clue.text: One who finishes, but not the first

definitions.text: One who finishes, but not the first

indicators.note: the first letter of the finisher word is left out

parts.note: a closer finishes, as a pitcher closing out a game

explanation.surface: Describing a runner who completes the race but does not win it.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue also defines the answer: someone who finishes the race but not first.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitor who completes the course without coming first has been beaten, so is a runner-up or worse.
